# Write a Polite Complaint Email to a Company with DeepSeek

> **In short:** DeepSeek can draft a polite, well-structured complaint email in under a minute — but you'll need to add the real details (order numbers, dates, names) and send it from your own account. It can't contact the company for you.

When something goes wrong with a product or service, the email you write in frustration usually gets ignored. A short, calm message that says what happened, what you want, and by when is far more likely to get a real reply. DeepSeek is great at shaping that kind of message — you describe the problem in your own words, and it turns your rambling into a clean, firm but polite email.

## Before you start
- A phone, tablet, or computer with internet access.
- A web browser (Chrome, Safari, Edge, Firefox — any modern one). Or the DeepSeek app if you prefer.
- A rough idea of what went wrong: when it happened, what you bought, and what you'd like the company to do about it.
- Any order numbers, receipts, or screenshots handy (helpful, but not required).
- About 10 to 15 minutes total.

## Step 1 — Open DeepSeek in your browser
Go to **chat.deepseek.com** in your web browser. The page loads a chat screen with a text box near the bottom labeled something like "Send a message" or "Message DeepSeek." No account is needed for a basic chat, so you can start typing right away. If you have the DeepSeek app installed, open it instead and you'll see the same chat layout.
💬 Example: type nothing yet — just confirm the box is there.
You'll know it worked when the chat screen is empty and ready, with a blinking cursor in the message box.

## Step 2 — Describe what happened in plain words
In the chat box, write a short, honest summary of the problem. Don't worry about grammar or politeness — just dump the facts the way you'd tell a friend. Include the company name, the product or service, when it happened, and what went wrong. DeepSeek reads everything in this message and uses it to draft the email later.
💬 Example: "I bought a coffee maker from BrewCo on March 12, order #44291. It arrived broken — the carafe was cracked and water leaks everywhere. I emailed them a week ago and nobody replied. I want a replacement or a full refund."
You'll know it worked when DeepSeek replies by asking a follow-up question or jumping straight into a draft. If it asks "What outcome do you want?", move to Step 3.

## Step 3 — Ask for a polite complaint email
Type a clear follow-up: "Please turn this into a polite complaint email I can send to the company. Keep it firm but respectful, around 150 words, with a subject line." DeepSeek now produces a full email — greeting, body paragraphs, and a sign-off — usually in a couple of seconds. The subject line usually appears at the top.
💬 Example: "Please turn this into a polite complaint email I can send to BrewCo customer service. Keep it firm but respectful, around 150 words, and give me a subject line too."
You'll know it worked when you see a complete email in the chat, with a "Subject:" line, a "Dear…" greeting, and a closing like "Sincerely."

## Step 4 — Tell DeepSeek what outcome you want
The first draft is usually generic. Tell DeepSeek specifically what you want the company to do — a refund, a replacement, an apology, a callback, a coupon. The clearer you are, the more useful the next draft becomes. You can also mention a reasonable deadline, like "within 7 business days."
💬 Example: "Please rewrite it so I clearly ask for a full refund of $89 within 7 business days, and mention that if I don't hear back I'll file a chargeback with my bank. Keep the same polite tone."
You'll know it worked when the new version includes your specific ask, in plain language, not a vague "I hope you can help."

## Step 5 — Adjust the tone if needed
Read the email out loud. Does it sound like you? If it's too stiff, say "make it sound warmer and more conversational." If it's too soft and you want to sound firmer, say "make the tone more direct without being rude." DeepSeek rewrites the whole email in seconds, so don't be shy about asking two or three times.
💬 Example: "Make it a bit warmer — I'm not angry, just disappointed. Keep the firmness but add one sentence saying I have liked their products in the past."
You'll know it worked when the new version feels like something you'd actually be comfortable sending under your own name.

## Step 6 — Add your real details and read it carefully
Now do the human part. Open the email in your own mail app (Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail — anything), and copy the draft over. Fill in the missing pieces: the actual recipient email (usually support@company.com or a contact form address), the real order number, dates, your name, and any return or tracking numbers. Read it once more to make sure it sounds like you and every fact is correct.
💬 Example: replace "[Your Name]" with your real name, "[Order #]" with the real order number, and double-check the dollar amounts.
You'll know it worked when the email reads as a complete, accurate message with no placeholder text like "[insert date here]."

## Step 7 — Send the email from your own account
Hit send from your own email account. DeepSeek can't send emails for you — it's a chat tool, not a mail program. After sending, keep the message handy; if you don't hear back in the time you mentioned (often 5 to 7 business days), you can simply reply to your own thread with "Just following up on my email below."
💬 Example: write a short follow-up — "Hi, I'm following up on my email from March 20 about order #44291. I haven't received a reply yet. Please let me know how you'd like to resolve this."
You'll know it worked when the email lands in your "Sent" folder and you have a copy you can quote later if needed.

## Common mistakes
- **Being too angry in the prompt.** DeepSeek often mirrors the tone of what you give it. If you rant, you may get a rant back. Stay matter-of-fact and let the tool do the polishing.
- **Forgetting the specific ask.** A complaint that doesn't say "refund, replacement, or reply by Friday" often gets a generic "we're sorry" reply. Always name what you want.
- **Sending without reading.** AI drafts sometimes invent details — a wrong date, a fake policy, a tone that isn't yours. Always read it once, top to bottom, before sending.
- **No receipt of what you sent.** Screenshot or forward the final email to yourself so you have proof of what was said and when.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** A broken toaster, a missed delivery, a noisy hotel room, a wrong phone bill — any of these can become a 10-minute fix instead of a week of ignored messages.
- **For your business or work:** If you invoice or buy from other companies, the same trick works for late payments, missing deliveries, or poor service. A polite, specific email usually beats a phone call.
- **If you're just getting started:** Pick the smallest, most recent annoyance and try one email. You'll see how much easier it is when you don't have to start from a blank page.

## Try it now
Think of one small frustration from the last month — a delayed package, a wrong charge, a rude reply from a store. Open DeepSeek, type two sentences about what happened, and ask it to turn that into a polite email. Read the draft, fix one detail, and save it in your drafts folder. You'll have a real, ready-to-send message in under five minutes.
